summary: Defines a MIB module for controlling the collection and storage of accounting information for connection-oriented networks such as ATM. It lets operators configure what usage data is gathered and how it is kept.

eli5.summary: This is the control panel for the usage counters: it lets a network manager choose what gets counted and where the tallies are stored.

questions: managed objects for collecting accounting information
what is the accounting control mib
how does snmp control accounting file collection
what happens when an accounting file is full
subtitle: SNMP controls for choosing what usage data a switch records and how it is filed.

tldr.problem: Switches in connection-oriented networks such as ATM can produce too much accounting data to fetch over SNMP, yet operators still need to control what is collected.
tldr.mechanism: A MIB module lets a manager select data items with (subtree, list) tuples, direct them into files, set when to collect, and swap files. The files are then retrieved with a file transfer protocol and use a standard BER format.
tldr.outcome: It is a Proposed Standard that is not obsoleted. It is network-independent, and RFC 2512 supplies the ATM data items to select.

facts.label: Trap threshold
facts.value: 0 to 99 percent; 0 means no nearly-full trap

today: RFC 2513 is a Proposed Standard from February 1999 and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The ATM data items it controls are defined in RFC 2512.

sections.title: Why Accounting Goes Into Files
sections.content:
RFC 2513 describes managed objects that control the collection and storage of accounting information for connection-oriented networks such as ATM. Administrators may need data on the bandwidth and resources used by connections, including switched (SVCs, SVPs), permanent (PVCs, PVPs) and soft-permanent (SPVCCs, SPVPCs) connections. The text says the need may also exist for other networks, such as Frame Relay.

The quantity of data is usually too large to fetch with SNMP, so the collected records are stored in a file and retrieved later with a file transfer protocol. SNMP is used only to control selection and collection. Particular data items are defined in other documents, such as RFC 2512 for ATM.
sections.eli5: The tally sheets are too big to read out loud over the phone, so the switch saves them in files you pick up later. The phone is only for giving instructions.

sections.title: The Operational Model
sections.content:
Switches collect data about connections routed across some of their interfaces. The data goes into one or more files, so for example PVC data can differ from SVC data.

To retrieve data, the administrator tells the switch to stop collecting into the current file and start a new one. The old file can then be fetched. A connection's set of objects and values is collected on one or more occasions:

  • when a connection is released, optionally including failed attempts;
  • periodically, for each active connection of a minimum age;
  • when a management application commands it, for each active connection of a minimum age.

The same set of objects is collected every time for a file, so object names are stored once at the start of the file and only values are stored in records. This gives a significantly smaller file.
sections.eli5: When you want the notes, you tell the switch to start a new notebook and hand you the old one. Because every page has the same columns, the column names are written only once.

sections.title: Full Files and Notifications
sections.content:
A file has a maximum size. When it passes a threshold percentage of that size, an SNMP notification such as a trap can optionally be sent, and another may be sent when the file is full. Two agent behaviours are allowed when a file fills:

  • Management application in control (swapOnCommand): the agent discards new data until the application tells it to swap. The application knows exactly which files exist, but data may be lost if it is late.
  • Agent swaps automatically (swapOnFull): the agent starts a new version of the same base file name with a changed suffix. The application must then check the file directory to see which suffixes were used.

Either way a finished file holds a whole number of connection records, so it ends just under or just over its maximum size.
sections.eli5: When the notebook is full you can either wait for a grown-up to give you a new one, or grab the next numbered notebook yourself. The first risks lost notes, the second means someone must check the shelf.

sections.title: Selection, File and Interface Controls
sections.content:
The module is ACCOUNTING-CONTROL-MIB at mib-2 60. Its objects fall in four groups: selection, file, interface and trap control.

The selection table has one row per (subtree, list) tuple, with an object saying which file the data goes to and an acctngSelectionType bit set for the connection types to cover. Changes to the table take effect only when collection next begins into a new file. A list is an OCTET STRING of up to 8 octets, where item 1 is the most significant bit of the first octet.

The file table names each file and holds its settings:

  • acctngFileCommand accepts swapToNewFile or collectNow when idle.
  • acctngFileMaximumSize defaults to 5000000 bytes.
  • acctngFileInterval (60 to 86400 seconds, default 3600) sets periodic collection.
  • acctngFileMinAge (60 to 86400 seconds, default 3600) sets the minimum connection age.
  • acctngFileCollectMode chooses onRelease and/or periodically.

Global objects include acctngAdminStatus, acctngOperStatus, acctngAgentMode and a per-interface acctngInterfaceEnable. acctngProtection guards against a duplicated SNMP message, such as a repeated swapToNewFile, causing a whole file of data to be lost.
sections.eli5: The control panel has switches for what to record, which notebook to use, how big it can get, how often to check, and a safety catch so a repeated message cannot throw a notebook away.

sections.title: The Collection File Format
sections.content:
The standard file is defined using ASN.1 and encoded with the Basic Encoding Rules (BER). The file has header information followed by zero or more connection records.

The header gives the switch's sysName, a textual description, the start time of the collection, and the sequence of (subtree, list) tuples. Each record holds the values for each tuple in the same order, and values within a tuple follow the order of the bits in the list. A checksum object, if selected, is first filled with zeros, then overwritten with the checksum calculated over the whole record.

The encoding is the same as in SNMPv2 with one exception: the indefinite length form is permitted for a SEQUENCE or SEQUENCE OF. The MIB also allows enterprise-specific formats, and acctngFileFormat uses ber(2) for the standard one.
sections.eli5: Each file starts with a cover page saying which switch, when, and what columns, followed by rows of values with no column names repeated.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
This MIB controls the collection of accounting data, so unauthorized access could disrupt it, possibly with fraudulent intent, for example by disabling collection or causing the wrong items to be collected.

SNMPv1 by itself is not a secure environment. The RFC recommends considering the SNMPv3 framework, specifically the User-based Security Model (RFC 2274) and the View-based Access Control Model (RFC 2275). Operators must configure the SNMP entity so only legitimate principals can GET or SET the objects.
sections.eli5: Whoever holds the control panel could secretly turn off the counting, so only trusted people should be allowed to touch it.

items.title: On release
items.text: A record is written when a connection ends, optionally including failed attempts.

items.title: Periodically
items.text: Active connections of a minimum age are recorded when a timer expires.

items.title: On command
items.text: A management application triggers collection with collectNow.
